harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory (mode 1777, root:root) so any user can create/write files but the sticky bit prevents non-owners from deleting each other's files. Verified functionally with two test users before and after a full node restart, and confirmed the restart via a changed kernel boot_id.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop, set ownership root:root and mode 1777 (world-writable + sticky bit)
Created two test users dropuser1 and dropuser2
Verified dropuser1 could write a file, and dropuser2 could write its own file but was denied (Operation not permitted) when attempting to delete dropuser1's file
Verified dropuser1 could delete its own file (owner deletion works normally)
Cleaned up test files, leaving /srv/drop empty with 1777 root:root
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and directory permissions
Issued a background 'shutdown -r now' on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed (55595e92... -> 84197775...), proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions (1777 root:root) persisted after restart
Re-ran the two-user write/delete test post-restart, confirming identical sticky-bit protection behavior and successful owner self-cleanup

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with correct ownership and sticky permissions
evidence.summary: mkdir + chown root:root + chmod 1777; stat confirms 1777 root:root /srv/drop

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: any user can write, but cannot remove another user's file (sticky bit enforcement)
evidence.summary: Created dropuser1/dropuser2; dropuser1 wrote a file; dropuser2 wrote its own file but rm on dropuser1's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' (rm_exit=1); owners could still clean up their own files

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity, not just elapsed time
evidence.summary: Connection timed out during reboot, then exec succeeded again; new boot_id=84197775-82c5-4f7b-8a29-168b1b19bbc9 differs from baseline, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit behavior
evidence.summary: /srv/drop still 1777 root:root after restart; repeated two-user write/delete test shows dropuser2 still denied deleting dropuser1's file while dropuser1 can delete its own, confirming full recovery
